events.title: Columbus Sights Dominica
events.description: On his second voyage to the New World, Christopher Columbus spotted a lush, mountainous island in the Caribbean on a Sunday morning. He named it Dominica, after the Latin word for Sunday.
events.significance: The sighting opened the Lesser Antilles to European exploration and colonization, and it began a long, often violent period of contact between Europe and the Caribbean.

events.title: Napoleon's Army Is Defeated at Vyazma
events.description: As the Grande Armée retreated from Moscow in worsening weather, Russian forces defeated its rear guard at the Battle of Vyazma.
events.significance: The defeat added to the attrition that wrecked Napoleon's invasion of Russia. It was one of the setbacks that eventually led to his downfall.

events.title: Panama Declares Independence
events.description: Panama broke away from Colombia in a swift and almost bloodless revolution. The United States quickly gave its support to the new nation.
events.significance: Independence cleared the way for the Panama Canal treaty and construction of the canal, which reshaped global trade and U.S. influence in Latin America.

events.title: William Howard Taft Wins the Presidency
events.description: Voters elected Taft, Theodore Roosevelt's chosen successor, as the 27th president of the United States.
events.significance: Taft later became the only person to serve as both U.S. president and Chief Justice of the United States.

events.title: Sputnik 2 Carries Laika Into Orbit
events.description: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 2 from Baikonur Cosmodrome. On board was Laika, a dog who became the first animal to orbit the Earth.
events.significance: The mission showed that a living creature could survive launch and weightlessness. That was an important early step toward human spaceflight, and it also raised ethical questions about animal testing.
